questions.text: The least number of squares to be added in the figure to make AB a line of symmetry is
questions.solution:
For AB to be a line of symmetry, every square must have its mirror image on the other side of AB.

- Left figure: 1 square above AB and 2 squares below (one just below the line on the left, one two rows down on the right). None of them has its mirror image [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] add 3.
- Right figure: 3 squares, all below AB [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] add their 3 mirror images above.

Total [latex]=3+3=6[/latex]

Answer: 6

questions.text:
A rectangular paper of 20cm x 8cm is folded 3 times. Each fold is made along the
line of symmetry, which is perpendicular to its long edge. The perimeter of the final
folded sheet (in cm) is
questions.solution:
Each fold halves the current longer side.

- 20 [latex]\times[/latex] 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fold [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10 [latex]\times[/latex] 8
- 10 [latex]\times[/latex] 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fold [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 [latex]\times[/latex] 8 (now 8 is the longer side)
- 5 [latex]\times[/latex] 8 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] fold [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 [latex]\times[/latex] 4

Perimeter [latex]=2(5+4)=18[/latex] cm.

Answer: 18

questions.text:
The pie chart presents the percentage contribution of different macronutrients to a typical 2,000 kcal diet of a person.

The typical energy density (kcal/g) of these macronutrients is given in the table.
[latex] \begin{array}{|l|c|} \hline Macronutrient & Energy density (kcal/g) \\ \hline Carbohydrates &4\\ \hline Proteins &4 \\ \hline Unsaturated fat &9 \\ \hline Saturated fat &9 \\ \hline Trans fat &9 \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]
The total fat (all three types), in grams, this person consumes is
questions.solution:
From the pie chart, fats = unsaturated 20% + saturated 20% + trans 5% = 45%.

Energy from fat [latex]=0.45\times2000=900[/latex] kcal.
All fats give 9 kcal/g, so fat [latex]=900/9=100[/latex] g.

Answer: 100

questions.text:
A rectangular paper sheet of dimensions 54cm x 4cm is taken. The two longer edges of the sheet are joined together to create a cylindrical tube. A cube whose surface area is equal to the area of the sheet is also taken.
Then, the ratio of the volume of the cylindrical tube to the volume of the cube is
questions.solution:
Joining the longer (54 cm) edges gives a tube of height 54 and circumference 4.
[latex]2\pi r=4\Rightarrow r=\dfrac{2}{\pi}[/latex], [latex]V_{cyl}=\pi r^2h=\pi\cdot\dfrac{4}{\pi^2}\cdot54=\dfrac{216}{\pi}[/latex]

Cube: [latex]6a^2=54\times4=216\Rightarrow a=6[/latex], [latex]V_{cube}=216[/latex]

Ratio [latex]=\dfrac{216/\pi}{216}=\dfrac{1}{\pi}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]1/\pi[/latex]

questions.text:
In the given text, the blanks are numbered (i)-(iv). Select the best match for all the blanks.
Steve was advised to keep his head ___(i)___ before heading __(ii)__ to bat; for, while he had a head __(iii)__ batting, he could only do so with a cool head s __(iv)__ his shoulders
questions.solution:
Meaning of each phrase:
- keep his head down [latex]\text{---}[/latex] stay low-profile / focused
- heading out to bat [latex]\text{---}[/latex] going out to the pitch
- a head for batting [latex]\text{---}[/latex] natural talent for it
- a cool head on his shoulders [latex]\text{---}[/latex] sensible and calm

Answer: (i) down (ii) out (iii) for (iv) on
